answer: Sybil resistance rests on stake-bound identity. Each agent must prove control of a funded account, so a thousand puppets cost a thousand funded accounts, not free keypairs. Registration locks that balance and reputation attaches to it, keeping capital illiquid. Every duplicate needs its own deposit, forfeited when peers catch a cluster voting as one voice. The ledger is a mirror: clones reveal shared funding and timing, and attestations count only from staked seats graded openly. Attacker cost scales with each fake, making every copy an expensive island rather than a cheap dune.
